name: The Cork Oak of Villa Siotto Pintor

official_register.name: Elenco degli alberi monumentali d'Italia (MASAF), Lombardia, sheet 01/E100/BG/03

access: View-only. The tree stands in the front garden of the closed Villa Siotto Pintor, directly on the public street (Via Vimercati Sozzi) and is seen through the portal gate. The villa interior opens only on FAI open days; a doorbell sign asks for visit requests by email. Do not enter the grounds.
transport: Montello-Gorlago railway station on the Bergamo-Brescia line (about 10 to 13 minutes by train from Bergamo per Trainline and e656 timetables); walk from station to Via Vimercati Sozzi not measured.

location_site.name: Front garden of Villa Siotto Pintor, Gorlago

story:
A Sardinian family brought this cork oak to the Bergamo plain, where the species is a rarity. It stands at the centre of the front garden of Villa Siotto Pintor in Gorlago, 18 metres tall and 320 centimetres round the trunk by the national register's measure, close enough to the street that the closed gate costs you nothing.

When it went in is a small dispute. Local tradition says 1861, the year the Kingdom of Italy was founded, which makes the neater story. The documents point to 1872, the year the Siotto Pintor family moved into the villa, and that puts the tree at roughly 150 years. Both versions agree it came with the family from Sardinia, where cork oak is at home.

The house behind it has changed hands several times, from the Lanzi to the Vimercati Sozzi, the name on the street outside, and finally to the Siotto Pintor. After the last descendant died it stood empty for years with its rooms left exactly as they were, wardrobes open and beds unmade, until urban explorers started photographing it. FAI opened it for its autumn open days in October 2020, with the oak still holding the middle of the old formal garden.

The rest of the year the grounds stay shut and the villa asks for visits by email. The tree does not need you inside. You see it through the portal gate, which is the whole visit and a good one.
how_to_recognise: You can recognise it as the cork oak at the centre of the villa's front garden, 18 metres tall. It stands behind the portal gate at Via Vimercati Sozzi 4, seen from the street.
verify_notes: Register: MASAF sheet 01/E100/BG/03, Quercus suber, girth 320 cm, height 18 m, altitude 237 m, Via Vimercati Sozzi 4, register coordinate 45.676439, 9.830014 (Wikidata Q55741741 carries 45.676531, 9.830186, about 20 m away: both inside the garden, so approximate). Register-only for dimensions; flagged: register only, no independent measurement found. Standing at the centre of the main front garden (giardino di rappresentanza) of the villa, the tree is a cork oak, an unusual species for the Bergamo plain. Both cosedibergamo (2020, author attended the October 2020 FAI opening) and FAI (Giornata FAI d'Autunno 2020) say it stands in the middle of the main garden and arrived with the Siotto Pintor family from Sardinia. Planting: cosedibergamo says tradition has it planted 1861 at the founding of the Kingdom of Italy, but documents point to a slightly later date, 1872, the year the Pintor family entered the villa; age therefore roughly 150 years (derived from a documented planting date for this specimen, given as tradition vs documents by the blog; not sharpened). Villa history: house of Guiscardo Lanzi (Grumelli), later Vimercati Sozzi, then Siotto Pintor; abandoned for years after the death of the last descendant, interiors left as they were (open wardrobes, unmade beds), explored by urbex photographers. FAI: beyond the closed gate one can admire the former representative garden. Alive: Commons photo File:Alberodasughero.jpg (Wiki Loves Monuments 2018, CC BY-SA 4.0, by Pattiferra, geotag 45.675883, 9.829439, about 72 m from the register point, taken from the street) is the Wikidata image for this register id; FAI page and cosedibergamo (Nov 2020) describe it standing. lifecheck.py returned NONE. Access/home risk: private villa, unoccupied; view-only from the public street, so the pin goes on the viewing place at the gate. Photograph exists (Commons WLM 2018, not yet judged, not hunted). Which trunk: the single central cork oak is the tree the register and FAI mean.
